SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.66
EXPLANATION: The intense band at 2123 cm⁻¹ is consistent with an internal alkyne C≡C stretch (typical ~2100–2140) rather than a nitrile (usually ~2240–2260), favoring an alkyne over nitrile candidates. Candidate 4 (CCC#CCCOC) contains an internal alkyne and an ether; its ether C–O–C stretches plausibly account for the 1108 and 1058 cm⁻¹ bands, while the aliphatic CH stretches at 2921/2880 and CH₂ scissoring at 1446 cm⁻¹ match general hydrocarbon features (GFQ-003). Absence of a ~3300 cm⁻¹ band disfavors terminal alkynes or alcohol OH (ruling out 3, 6, 7, 9), and the 2123 cm⁻¹ position is too low for a C≡N stretch (ruling out 1, 5, 8, 10). Candidate 2 (isothiocyanate) is less consistent with the observed ether-like 1108/1058 cm⁻¹ pair.
